title: Daniil Medvedev snaps Carlos Alcaraz win streak for Indian Wells final against Jannik Sinner
content:
INDIAN WELLS, Calif. — Daniil Medvedev got his revenge Saturday in the searing heat of the Coachella Valley, beating world No. 1 Carlos Alcaraz , 6-3, 7-6(3), after losing to the Spaniard in back-to-back BNP Paribas Open finals in 2023 and 2024.

Medvedev will play his first ATP Masters 1000 final in two years Sunday against Jannik Sinner, who beat Alexander Zverev in a straightforward, 6-2, 6-4 first semifinal earlier on Saturday.

With the win — his first over Alcaraz since the 2023 U.S. Open semifinals — world No. 11 Medvedev also returns to the top 10 for the first time since July, on the back of a performance that blended his vintage hard-court mastery with all-out attack, and the belief that he could push himself to the limits against the best player in the world, who had not lost all year.

He was in control from the start of Saturday’s semifinal — no small feat against Alcaraz — as the court and the hot conditions suited his big serve and flat power. Alcaraz also leant him an assist, by being not as sharp as usual at net and just a hair slower in his reaction time at the baseline.

Medvedev zipped to a 4-1 lead with little trouble, and Alcaraz didn’t have a break point in the first set.

The 30-year-old from Russia is experiencing something of a renaissance at the start of 2026. He won the Brisbane International January in Australia, and picked up another title at the Dubai Tennis Championships earlier this month.

The latter, a walk-over win in the final against Tallon Griekspoor, meant he was stuck in the city for several days, due to the United States and Israel’s strikes on Iran and retaliatory strikes by Iran on the United Arab Emirates and other neighboring nations in West Asia.

Medvedev’s hot streak continued when he arrived in Indian Wells, and he has breezed through the draw without dropping a set, including dispatching defending champion Jack Draper in the quarterfinals.

There was a small controversy, when Medvedev requested a video review of Draper making a shrugging motion mid-point. He was successful, even though he and Draper had continued to play the point out, and Medvedev requested a review only after he had sent a backhand into the net.

Whatever the outcome of that point, Medvedev only looked like winning the match, and the same was true Saturday. Alcaraz finally found a foothold in the second set after taking several big steps back on his return position to allow himself more time, but Medvedev’s level did not let up all match, even as Alcaraz broke for a 3-1 lead. Medvedev got the break back immediately, and made it to a tiebreak in which he took control once again. Medvedev took a 6-1 lead, and though Alcaraz saved two match points to make it 6-3, Medvedev sealed victory with an ace.

He was through to his biggest final in two years, and Alcaraz had his first loss of the season.
